ServiceApproach.label: Our Method
ServiceApproach.body: Build the systems that regulated industries and critical enterprises depend on — through engineering precision, deep domain context, and an unwavering commitment to outcomes that endure long after deployment.
ServiceApproach.story_intro: In financial services, a delayed transaction is a questioned transaction. We asked: what if compliance checking could run faster than the transaction itself?
ServiceApproach.story_p1: Working alongside a regional bank managing high-frequency payment flows across six markets, we built a real-time compliance engine that screens every transaction against live regulatory rule sets in under 50 milliseconds. The system ingests jurisdiction-specific data, applies institution-defined thresholds, and flags anomalies before funds clear — not after.
ServiceApproach.story_p2: This was not a matter of tuning an existing vendor tool. We designed the architecture from scratch around a single constraint: compliance at the speed of commerce. Every decision — from data pipeline design to alert triage logic — was made with that constraint as the governing principle.
ServiceApproach.story_p3: Today, the platform processes over three million transactions daily with no production downtime since launch. More importantly, it gave the bank's compliance team a system they could explain to regulators, operate with confidence, and extend as requirements evolve. That is what we mean when we say we build to last.

financial-institutions.claim: ScaleJade builds the layer between a core banking system that cannot be taken offline and a settlement deadline that will not move.
financial-institutions.card_summary: Core banking integration, real-time screening, and reporting an examiner can follow end to end.
financial-institutions.intro: Indonesian banks are absorbing BI-FAST settlement, QRIS interoperability and tightening AML reporting at the same time — usually on core systems that predate all three and cannot be taken offline to find out what breaks.

pressures.title: Settlement windows that do not move
pressures.desc: BI-FAST clears in seconds, and the window does not care that your core is mid-batch. Throughput has to hold at the worst minute of the month, not the average one.

pressures.title: Cores older than the rules they now satisfy
pressures.desc: QRIS interoperability and SNAP open APIs are being asked of systems specified a decade before either existed — and there is no maintenance window long enough to find out what breaks.

pressures.title: Screening that has to clear before the money does
pressures.desc: APU-PPT obligations put a compliance check inside the payment path. Every millisecond it costs is a millisecond taken from settlement.

systems.title: Core banking integration layers
systems.desc: Adapters and anti-corruption layers that let new services talk to a core you are not permitted to modify.

systems.title: Real-time AML and sanctions screening
systems.desc: Screening inside the payment path, measured at p99 under production load rather than in a benchmark.

systems.title: Regulatory reporting pipelines
systems.desc: Reporting an examiner can follow from the ledger entry to the submitted figure without a spreadsheet in the middle.

systems.title: Settlement and reconciliation systems
systems.desc: Deterministic finality, and a reconciliation story that still holds when a downstream system disagrees.

financial-institutions.cta_title: Working on a core migration, a screening path, or a reporting obligation?

public-sector.claim: ScaleJade builds systems that survive the handover — documented, auditable, and owned by the institution rather than the vendor.
public-sector.card_summary: Systems a public institution can still operate in ten years, without the vendor that built them.
public-sector.intro: Public sector technology in Indonesia now has to satisfy SPBE architecture requirements, national data centre residency, and UU PDP — while remaining operable by teams who will still be running it in ten years.

pressures.title: Architecture decided before delivery starts
pressures.desc: SPBE sets the shape of the system, so interoperability and data model decisions are made at procurement. Getting them wrong is not something a later sprint fixes.

pressures.title: Residency constrains the design, not just the contract
pressures.desc: Pusat Data Nasional requirements decide where the data sits, which decides the failover story, which decides the architecture.

pressures.title: The handover is the deliverable
pressures.desc: A system the institution cannot operate without the vendor that built it has not been delivered. It has been rented.

systems.title: Interoperability layers between agencies
systems.desc: Shared services and APIs built to the SPBE data model, so the next agency to connect does not need a bespoke integration.

systems.title: Citizen data platforms under UU PDP
systems.desc: Consent, retention and access logging designed into the data model rather than retrofitted after the first audit.

systems.title: Sovereign and on-premise deployments
systems.desc: Infrastructure that satisfies residency requirements without giving up the operational tooling a modern team expects.

systems.title: Documentation and handover packages

education-research.claim: ScaleJade builds the data infrastructure underneath — and publishes the evaluation work, including the parts that did not flatter the model.
education-research.card_summary: Student data infrastructure, and published benchmarks for the AI tools institutions are being asked to evaluate.
education-research.intro: Universities hold some of the most sensitive personal data in the country on some of the oldest systems, and are now being asked to evaluate AI tools nobody has benchmarked for their languages or their teaching.

pressures.title: The most sensitive data on the oldest systems
pressures.desc: Student records fall squarely under UU PDP, and they usually live in systems built before anyone had to think about consent or retention.

pressures.title: AI tools nobody has benchmarked for you
pressures.desc: Institutions are asked to evaluate tutoring and assessment tools scored on English answer accuracy — which says almost nothing about whether they can teach in Bahasa Indonesia.

pressures.title: Reporting that has to reconcile
pressures.desc: PDDIKTI submissions have to agree with the systems of record, which is harder than it sounds once three departments each keep their own.

systems.title: Student data platforms under UU PDP

systems.title: Language model evaluation for teaching
systems.desc: Benchmarks and rubrics that measure pedagogy rather than answer accuracy. TutorBench is ours, and it is published.

systems.title: Southeast Asian language data practice
systems.desc: Human data collection and annotation for Bahasa Indonesia and regional languages — training and evaluation sets built by people who speak them.

systems.title: Reporting and records integration
systems.desc: PDDIKTI and internal reporting reconciled against one system of record instead of three.

education-research.cta_title: Evaluating an AI tool, or modernising student records?
education-research.cta_body: We publish our evaluation work. Read it first, then tell us what you are actually trying to measure.

items.title: Most core banking systems predate the regulations they now have to satisfy
items.body: BI-FAST settlement, QRIS interoperability and tightening AML reporting all arrived after the systems that have to carry them. The usual fix — a vendor module bolted to the side — fails for a structural reason: it can't be tuned inside the settlement window, and the core can't be taken offline to find out what breaks. That gap between the regulation and the system is where ScaleJade works.

items.title: The firms that can do the engineering don't know the regulation
items.body: Domain knowledge and delivery capability are usually held by different companies, which is why so much regulated work arrives as a subcontract two layers down from whoever signed the contract. Our engineers have run production systems under these rules. The person who scopes your engagement is the person who builds it.

items.title: A model evaluated in English tells you nothing about how it performs in Bahasa Indonesia
items.body: Benchmarks that decide procurement are almost entirely English-language, and the gap between benchmark performance and behaviour in Southeast Asian languages is not small. ScaleJade runs a dedicated human-data practice for training and evaluating models in Bahasa Indonesia and the region's languages, and publishes the benchmarks.
